claims.explanation: MG-132 is a proteasome inhibitor, so selectivity likely reflects dependence on proteasome-mediated degradation of pro-survival or anti-apoptotic factors, particularly NF-kB signaling and HIF-1alpha turnover. Lines with high NF-kB activity or mutations that increase reliance on proteasomal degradation (e.g., TP53, KRAS, BRAF, PIK3CA) are more sensitive, while those with low proteasome dependence or alternative survival pathways are less affected.

features.basis: MG-132 blocks IkB degradation, inhibiting constitutive NF-kB survival signaling in sensitive lines
MG-132 stabilizes HIF-1alpha, and high HIF1A may create proteotoxic stress or alter metabolism
TP53 mutations are frequent in sensitive lines, possibly due to loss of p53-mediated adaptation to proteasome inhibition
KRAS-mutant lines are enriched among sensitive lines, suggesting oncogenic KRAS increases proteasome dependence
BRAF mutations appear in several sensitive lines, possibly via MAPK-driven proteasome addiction
PIK3CA mutations are common in sensitive lines, linking PI3K/AKT survival signaling to proteasome dependence
NFE2L2 mutations in sensitive esophageal lines may impair antioxidant response, increasing proteasome inhibitor toxicity
ARID1A mutations appear in multiple sensitive lines, possibly altering chromatin and stress responses
PTEN mutations are more common in least-affected lines, suggesting intact PTEN or PI3K signaling may protect
STK11 mutations appear in several resistant lines, possibly indicating metabolic adaptation to proteasome inhibition
ALK alterations in resistant neuroblastoma and mesothelioma lines may provide alternative survival signaling
CDKN2A mutations are frequent in resistant lines, possibly reflecting cell cycle-independent survival
